inputs.original_text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff as the district faces a budget shortfall and cuts of more than 70 positions. It’s a painful situation, especially for the families and employees affected—but calling every shortfall proof that schools simply need more money is too easy. School leaders owe parents and taxpayers a clear account of how resources are being managed before asking the community to accept more cuts or bigger costs. Children and dedicated staff shouldn’t be left to bear the consequences of poor decisions.
inputs.modified_text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff as the district faces cuts of more than 70 positions. Families and dedicated employees shouldn’t be made to carry the burden while school leaders avoid explaining how the money was managed. Before taxpayers are asked to pay more, the district owes them clear answers and responsible stewardship. Asking for more funding can’t be the automatic answer to every shortfall.
